steps: Confirm your Electrician license is active and in good standing in Florida.
Submit a license verification request from Florida through the appropriate national registry or the state board directly.
File an application for full new application required with Texas's licensing board.
Register for and pass the required exam: TDLR Journeyman Electrician Exam, administered by PSI.
Complete 32 additional training/CE hours required by Texas.
Pay the Texas application fee (approx. $235) and submit supporting documents.
Await processing — typically 30-90 days in Texas.
notes: Texas (TDLR) has electrical reciprocity agreements with only a short, specific list of states (Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Nebraska, New Mexico, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Wyoming) - none of which include California, Florida, New York, or Ohio. Applicants from those four states must apply as a new, non-reciprocal applicant: $30 journeyman application fee plus a $78 PSI exam fee ($108 total), and TDLR may still require documented supervised on-the-job hours even for an already-licensed electrician, not just a fee and paperwork.
officialSourceName: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR)
